nodes.description: Targeted Gjb3 replacement produced homozygous null mice. Many homozygous embryos were lost during placental development, but surviving adults had no reported morphological or functional defect of the inner ear or skin. Placental recovery coincided with increased Cx43 expression; compensation in adult tissues was the authors' interpretation. This null genotype does not test a heterozygous variant with toxic or dominant-interfering effects. Normal null skin is not a failed test of every dominant EKV mechanism.

The founding report associated heterozygous missense and nonsense GJB3 variants with hearing loss in two families. GJB3 encodes connexin 31. Selected variants have measurable effects in expression systems, but clinical pathogenicity and penetrance remain disputed; heterozygosity alone does not establish causation or select among dosage, dominant-negative and toxic gain-of-function mechanisms. The frequently screened c.538C>T (p.Arg180*) allele lacked significant enrichment in subsequent case-control studies.

nodes.description: Selected mutants reduce intercellular dye transfer or ionic coupling in heterologous expression systems. V27M and V84I did not function normally when coexpressed with wild-type Cx31; this does not independently establish dominant-negative action or clinical pathogenicity. V174M did not form functional dye-transferring channels and interfered with Cx26 trafficking while sparing Cx31 wild-type trafficking. Mouse localization and rat transcript data support auditory expression, not direct demonstration of gap-junction coupling between inner hair cells or spiral ganglion neurons.
